summary: This article explains how date palms survive in hot, dry places, how people use nearly every part of the tree, how farmers pollinate and harvest dates, and why dates are a healthy food.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “The Date Palm: Tree of the Desert” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: a green place in a desert where there is water
a long, strong piece of wood or metal that holds up part of a building

challengeTerms.def: very dry, with very little rain
changed over time to fit well in a certain place
to plant and care for crops so they grow

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the date palm is the most useful tree in the desert? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how farmers help date palms produce a good crop of dates.
struggling: Pre-teach oasis, beam, and produce with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses arid, adapted, and cultivate to suggest a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
